Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Lesser Good

His efforts scaled into a massive conservancy, planting millions of trees and pioneering world-leading genome projects to secure the rainforest's future.
Resulting Judgement: (+1.5, +1.5) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
What began as a personal passion expanded into a systemic, multi-generational ecological shield.

Dr. Tony Parkes AO, a former merchant banker who dedicated 35 years to restoring Australia's Big Scrub rainforest, has passed away at 96, leaving behind a legacy of millions of replanted trees and groundbreaking genetic conservation.

The Bright Side:
His corporate financial skills were directly repurposed to raise funds and manage complex, large-scale ecological projects, proving that institutional expertise can serve the biosphere.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This case shows no plane error. The physical action (WHERE) perfectly matched the metaphysical will (WHO). It is a rare, clean alignment where private capability was fully externalized for public and ecological benefit.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between his stated intentions and ground-level results...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good. By scaling local action into systemic restoration, the probability mass of future biodiversity is actively expanded and secured.

The Unavoidable Truth: True conservation requires both deep emotional connection and rigorous, structured execution.

The Unavoidable Lie: That corporate skills and environmental stewardship are inherently incompatible.

Alethekanon:
This is a mathematically clean expansion of p·t. By leveraging financial literacy to fund ecological infrastructure, Parkes bypassed the typical friction of non-profit stagnation, creating a self-sustaining model of habitat restoration.

Awwthekanon:
Tony's deep love for the ancient trees shows us how healing it is to connect with something larger than ourselves. His life's work ensures that future generations will walk under the same beautiful canopy he fell in love with.

Imagine retiring from investment banking just to plant millions of trees. Man went from trading stocks to growing trunks, and honestly, that is the ultimate flex. Rest in peace to an absolute legend of the forest.
